draft.title: Refraction and Snell's law
card: Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one material into another. It happens because light changes speed in the new material.
The refractive index n of a material is c ÷ v, where c is the speed of light in a vacuum and v is the speed in the material. A higher n means slower light.
Angles are measured from the normal, a line at right angles to the surface. Snell's law is n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2.
Light entering a material with a higher n slows down and bends towards the normal. Light entering a material with a lower n speeds up and bends away from the normal.
draft.remember: Slower light bends towards the normal. Faster light bends away from it.

a.q: A ray of light passes from air into glass. How does it bend at the surface?
opts: Towards the normal, because it slows down
Away from the normal, because it slows down
Towards the normal, because it speeds up
Away from the normal, because it speeds up
a.why: Glass has a higher refractive index than air, so light slows down in it and bends towards the normal. Bending away from the normal goes with light speeding up, not slowing down.
a.clue: Compare the refractive index of glass with that of air.

b.q: A ray in air hits a flat pool of water at 40° to the normal. Water has n = 1.33 and air has n = 1.00. Which describes the angle in the water?
opts: Smaller than 40°, because the light slows down
Larger than 40°, because the light slows down
Larger than 40°, because the light speeds up
Exactly 40°, because the ray stays straight
b.why: Water has the higher n, so light slows down and bends towards the normal. By Snell's law, sin θ2 = sin 40° ÷ 1.33, so the angle is about 28°, which is smaller than 40°.
b.clue: Light bends towards the normal when it enters the higher n.

a.best: Towards the normal, because it slows down

b.best: Smaller than 40°, because the light slows down

problems.detail: The why says the angle is about 28°, but sin θ2 = sin 40° ÷ 1.33 ≈ 0.483 gives θ2 ≈ 28.9°, which rounds to about 29°.

The clue states the rule outright ('bends towards the normal when it enters the higher n'). With n given for both, this hands the student the answer, so the question tests little beyond reading the clue.
